cohort: 213 singleton pregnancies diagnosed with placenta previa using antenatal ultrasonographic examination in a tertiary reference hospital between January 2014 and December 2015.
finding: The coexistence of placenta previa-accreta was associated with increased maternal-neonatal morbidity, while low-lying, marginal, and partial PP, compared to complete PP, did not result in increased morbidity.
birth_weight: Measured, but no specific finding reported
